slides.eyebrow: Both an Asset and a Risk
slides.title: Autonomy Cuts Both Ways
bullets: MSLs manage their own calendar with limited daily oversight
One of the most attractive features of the role
Also one of the biggest risks without deliberate prioritisation

slides.title: Protect the Territory Plan, Don't Reinvent It
bullets: Good time management starts with the territory plan from Lesson 4
Prioritisation becomes protecting that plan, not inventing it weekly
Without it, the calendar fills with whoever asks first or feels urgent

slides.title: Urgent Is Not the Same as Important
bullets: An unsolicited medical information request is genuinely urgent
Quarterly reviews and thorough insight write-ups are important, not urgent
Important tasks get pushed aside under pressure unless protected deliberately

slides.title: Manage Travel and Geography Deliberately
bullets: Cluster visits by region instead of crossing the territory back and forth
Be honest about the real time cost of high-effort activities
Include recovery time for things like international congresses

slides.title: Protect Time to Reflect and Synthesise
bullets: Time to read the papers relevant to upcoming conversations
Time to properly write up insights, not just log raw notes
Time to check whether current activity still matches territory priorities

slides.eyebrow: Why It Matters for Your Career
slides.title: A Predictor of Advancement
bullets: Time management and self-discipline predict who moves into leadership
Higher-level roles demand even greater self-directed prioritisation
With larger scale and less structure imposed from above

takeaway.title: Autonomy only pays off when it is spent deliberately, not reactively
bullets: The territory plan, not the inbox, should set the week's priorities
Important work needs protected time or it loses out to urgent work
Self-discipline with time is a clear predictor of career advancement
